chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abu Ayyub, who said:

Muhammad ibn Muslim asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) while I was listening: 'If a traveler intends to stay for ten days, he should complete the prayer.' He said: 'If he does not know whether he will stay for a day or more, he should count thirty days, then complete, even if he stayed for a day or one prayer.' Muhammad ibn Muslim said to him: 'It has reached me that you said five [days].' He said: 'I have indeed said that.' Abu Ayyub said: 'I said, may I be your ransom, can it be less than five days?' He said: 'No.' Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: 'What this report entails regarding the command to complete [prayer] if one intends to stay for five days is understood to apply when one is in Mecca or Medina. What indicates that is what has been narrated:'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on shortening prayer if a traveler intends to stay for ten days or less?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the jurisprudential debate regarding the threshold for shortening prayers, specifically addressing the discrepancy between the general ten-day rule and the five-day rule often cited for Mecca and Medina. It highlights the scholarly nuance that while ten days is the baseline for maintaining traveler status, specific locations like Mecca may require completing prayers even for shorter durations, a point emphasized by Imam al-Sadiq's confirmation of the five-day precedent.
